questions.answer: For Northbay repair cases evaluated on 2026-07-01, closure is permitted if and only if identity verification is complete, no active hold exists, and either the routine documentary packet is complete or all three exception conditions hold: minor-repair scope, complete exception reconciliation, and register-defined authorization. These are the exhaustive routes; the routine route requires no exception approval. Unavailable facts are unknown, not false. Under three-valued logic an AND is false if any child is false, otherwise unknown if any child is unknown; an OR is true if any child is true, otherwise unknown if any child is unknown; NOT preserves unknown. Thus unavailable evidence need not make the overall result unknown if another operand determines it.

The exception route requires minor-repair scope, completed exception reconciliation, and authorization under the approval-register definition. These three conditions are jointly necessary and sufficient for the exception route itself. It does not waive identity verification or the requirement that no active hold exist.

Authorization is true exactly when the register records an unrevoked approval by a duty supervisor with a matching case identifier. Explicit register rejection or revocation makes authorization false; unavailable required register evidence makes it unknown (null), not false. Requester email, vendor signature, or an inferred job title does not establish register authorization. False authorization defeats the exception route, whereas missing authorization can leave that route unknown unless another exception condition is false. Neither alone determines overall closure because the routine route is independent of exception approval.

No. On 2026-07-01 the April Northbay decision and its annex restrict the exception to minor repairs, so even valid supervisor approval cannot make a major repair eligible. A major repair may still qualify via the routine route with verified identity and no active hold. The signed June 20 decision expands exception scope only from 2026-10-01; publication does not activate that expansion early. The broader 2025 rule expired and was replaced. Southbay rules cannot amend Northbay rules, and the refund policy does not govern repair closure. Those different dates and scopes cannot establish eligibility here.

No. The June 25 version-3 memorandum proposes dropping reconciliation, allowing team-lead authorization, and reviewing holds after closure, but it is an unsigned, unapproved discussion draft with no effective date; circulation is not enactment. Existing signed decisions remain in force. The vendor recommendation to close after payment and a technician signature is only a supplier workflow preference and has no authority to amend board rules; its shipment acceptance is not register authorization. The governing April decision expressly excludes amendment by either source. Therefore exception reconciliation and the no-active-hold requirement remain binding. Payment alone is insufficient. The historical 2025 payment rule does not continue, and even the signed October-effective decision leaves identity and hold conditions unchanged and still requires reconciliation.
